课程简介（中文）

本课程围绕数列极限、一元函数微分与积分展开, 主要内容有：

集合与映射，数列极限,函数极限，连续函数，导数与微分,微分中值定理,Taylor 展开式, 不定积分, 定积分,反常积分,常微分方程.

课程简介（英文）

This course is mainly focused on limit and calculus for one variable functions. In its contents we have:

Set and mapping, The limit of sequences, The limit of functions, Continuous functions, Derivatives and differentiation, The mean value theorems, The Taylor expansions, Indefinite integrals, Definite integrals, Improper integrals, Ordinary differential equations.

教学目标

为新工科类和管理学类本科学生进入下一阶段专业课尤其是分析类课程的学习,打下基础。进一步加强学生的逻辑思维、抽象思维能力,注重培植学生的自主学习能力与初步的研究能力。

This course lays a foundation for undergraduate students in new engineering and management disciplines to move on to the next stage of specialized courses, especially analytical courses. It further strengthens students’ logical thinking and abstract thinking abilities, and focuses on cultivating their autonomous learning ability and preliminary research ability.

教学方式

授课

教学内容与进度安排

Week 1 (6 class hours):
Chapter 1 Sets, Russell's paradox, countable sets, uncountable sets, Cartesian product, mappings and functions. Chapter 2 Supremum Existence Theorem.

Week 2 (6 class hours):
Limits of sequences, properties of limits, infinitely large quantities.

Week 3 (6 class hours):
Indeterminate forms; fundamental theorems of the real number system: Monotone Bounded Theorem, Nested Interval Theorem, Bolzano-Weierstrass Theorem, Cauchy Convergence Criterion.

Week 4 (6 class hours):
Chapter 3 Limits of functions: definitions and properties, Heine Theorem, two important limits.

Week 5 (6 class hours):
Continuous functions and their properties.

Week 6 (6 class hours):
Equivalence relations; Boundedness Theorem for continuous functions on a closed interval, Extreme Value Theorem, Intermediate Value Theorem, uniform continuity.

Week 7 (6 class hours):
Chapter 4 Differentials and derivatives, the four arithmetic rules of differentiation, differentiation of composite functions.

Week 8 (6 class hours):
Differentiation of inverse functions, implicit functions, and functions defined by parametric equations; higher-order derivatives; Leibniz formula for higher-order derivatives.

Week 9 (6 class hours):
Midterm exam (time to be arranged separately); Chapter 5 Fermat's Theorem, Rolle's Mean Value Theorem, Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem, Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem, monotonicity.

Week 10 (6 class hours):
Convexity and concavity of functions, Jensen's inequality, L'Hôpital's Rule, Taylor expansion, polynomial interpolation.

Week 11 (6 class hours):
Applications of derivatives, extremum problems of functions, curve sketching; Chapter 6 Definition of indefinite integrals, integration by substitution of the first type, integration by substitution of the second type, integration by parts.

Week 12 (6 class hours):
Indefinite integrals of rational functions, indefinite integrals of trigonometric rational functions; Chapter 7 Definition of definite integrals, necessary and sufficient conditions for Riemann integrability, classes of integrable functions.

Week 13 (6 class hours):
First Mean Value Theorem for Integrals, Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, computation of definite integrals: substitution, integration by parts, use of symmetry.

Week 14 (6 class hours):
Applications of definite integrals; Chapter 8 Improper integrals: definition and computation, Cauchy criterion for improper integrals, comparison test.

Week 15 (6 class hours):
(This part will be covered in the courseware and reference books.) Basic concepts and terminology of differential equations; common solution methods: separation of variables, integrating factor method, first-order linear equations, substitution method, reduction of order.

Week 16 (6 class hours):
Higher-order linear equations with constant coefficients, characteristic equation, fundamental system of solutions, general solution, method of undetermined coefficients for nonhomogeneous higher-order linear equations with constant coefficients.

Week 17 and Week 18 (Final Exam)
